header: This is the "learned pattern" half of the hybrid router (29 Sep 2026, see chat): once the LLM successfully classifies and grounds a genuinely new phrasing, its generalized shape (ParsedIntent.patternTemplate, e.g. "list all names ends with {name}") is persisted here. On every future query I check this cache BEFORE the LLM is called at all: a hit means the same phrasing shape, with a different name/department/ designation, gets answered instantly and for free, the same way a hand-written deterministic parser rule would, except that this "rule" was derived by the LLM from real usage instead of hand-coded in advance. I keep this deliberately as a SEPARATE table from anything hand-coded. It only ever grows from confirmed-successful LLM classifications (see queryOrchestrator.ts's learning condition), never from a guess, and it never overrides the deterministic parser or the grounding layers underneath: a cache hit still goes through the exact same resolveDesignationTerm/resolveSailDepartment/rosterQuery grounding as everything else, just with the free-text extraction step skipped.

symbols.name: compileTemplate
doc: Compiles a template like "how many {designation} in {department}" into a case-insensitive regex with named capture groups.

symbols.name: matchLearnedPattern
symbols.sig: export async function matchLearnedPattern(query: string): Promise<PatternMatch | null>
doc: Checks the learned-pattern cache for a match. It is fast: one cached query, then a handful of in-memory regex tests, with no LLM call involved.

symbols.name: fillTemplate
symbols.sig: export function fillTemplate( shape: ParsedIntent, captures: Partial<Record<PlaceholderField, string>>,): ParsedIntent
doc: Fills a cached shape's placeholders with values captured from a new query and produces a concrete ParsedIntent, with no LLM call involved.

symbols.name: isTemplateConsistent
doc: Validates that a parsed intent's patternTemplate is internally consistent: the placeholder actually appears for whichever field was populated, and no placeholder appears for a field that is null. I would rather never cache a pattern than cache an inconsistent template, which would silently produce wrong answers every time it matched.

symbols.name: learnPatternPending
symbols.sig: export async function learnPatternPending(parsed: ParsedIntent): Promise<number | null>
doc: Inserts a NEWLY classified-and-grounded intent's generalized template as a PENDING pattern, NOT yet matchable by matchLearnedPattern. It only becomes usable once a person explicitly confirms it (tick) via recordPatternFeedback below. It returns the new row's id so the caller can attach it to the response for the frontend to reference when feedback comes back. It also returns the id of an EXISTING pending row when the same template + identical shape is asked again. It returns null when the template is inconsistent, the existing row is already decided (confirmed/rejected), or the existing row holds a DIFFERENT shape.

symbols.name: PatternFeedback
doc: Feedback on a pending pattern. ONLY an explicit tick/cross is accepted.

My decision, 29 Sep 2026 (permanent): inferred signals such as how long an answer stayed on screen are removed entirely. Reading a confidently WRONG answer for several seconds looks identical to reading a right one, so an inferred signal could promote a misread pattern and serve it to everyone. A pattern becomes matchable only when a person says it is correct.

symbols.name: recordPatternFeedback
symbols.sig: export async function recordPatternFeedback(patternId: number, feedback: PatternFeedback): Promise<void>
doc: Records a person's explicit verdict on a pending pattern. It is decisive and immediate. It only ever changes a row that is still 'pending', so a later click can't flip an already-decided pattern.

symbols.name: recordPatternHit
doc: Fire-and-forget: bumps hit_count/last_used_at on a TIER-2 cache hit (i.e. the pattern was already 'confirmed' and got used again). It is a separate concern from the pending/confirmed feedback lifecycle above. The caller never awaits it: a failure here must never affect the response.
